title: Cold rebuild: ParseAdd
summary: Rebuild the sk add parser from memory: list patterns, flags and a record.

steps.title: Rebuild it from memory
body: Before the boss, prove that **ParseAdd** survived. This step is a *cold rebuild*:
- the editor starts **empty**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at;
- the tests are **exactly** the ones your Sidekick piece passed;
- it is short: one piece, from the spec alone.
Why: pulling something out of memory (instead of re-reading it) is what makes it stick. If you get stuck, that is
useful information, not failure: go back to the lesson, then come back here tomorrow.

steps.prompt: In a `switch (rest)` over the remaining arguments, where must `case [var flag, ..] when flag.StartsWith("-"): return null;` go?
options: After the `--tag`, `--project` and `--est` cases, before the plain-word case
Anywhere: the order of cases does not matter
steps.explain: The first matching case wins. Known flags must match first; a plain-word case placed before it would swallow `--colour` as part of the title.

steps.title: Cold: ParseAdd
prompt: - `record AddRequest(string Title, string? Tag, string? Project, int EstimateMinutes);`
- `static AddRequest? ParseAdd(string[] args)`: list patterns over the arguments: `--tag`/`-t`, `--project`/`-p`,
`--est`/`-e` (parsed by `Sk.TryParseMinutes`; unparseable means `null`), any other `-` word means `null`, other
words join into the trimmed title; no title means `null`.
- `static TaskItem AddTask(Assistant assistant, AddRequest request)`: add title and estimate, then set `Tag` and
`Sk.TryParseMinutes`, `TaskItem`, `Assistant` and `MemoryStore` are given. Functions first, then the record.
solution: string? title = null, tag = null, project = null;
case ["--tag" or "-t", var t, .. var tail]:
case ["--project" or "-p", var p, .. var tail]:
case ["--est" or "-e", var e, .. var tail]:
title = title is null ? word : title + " " + word;
return string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(title) ? null : new AddRequest(title.Trim(), tag, project, estimate);
static TaskItem AddTask(Assistant assistant, AddRequest request)
record AddRequest(string Title, string? Tag, string? Project, int EstimateMinutes);
template: Dojo.Eq("two words make one title", new AddRequest("Fix login", null, null, 0), ParseAdd(new[] { "Fix", "login" }));
Dojo.Eq("--tag and --est", new AddRequest("Fix login redirect", "bug", null, 90), ParseAdd(new[] { "Fix login redirect", "--tag", "bug", "--est", "1h30" }));
Dojo.Eq("short flags in any order", new AddRequest("Fix login", "bug", "web", 45), ParseAdd(new[] { "-p", "web", "Fix login", "-t", "bug", "-e", "45m" }));
Dojo.Eq("the title is trimmed", new AddRequest("Docs", null, "core", 0), ParseAdd(new[] { "  Docs ", "--project", "core" }));
Dojo.Check("an estimate that is not a time gives null", ParseAdd(new[] { "Fix", "--est", "soon" }) is null);
Dojo.Check("a flag with no value gives null", ParseAdd(new[] { "Fix", "--tag" }) is null);
Dojo.Check("an unknown flag gives null", ParseAdd(new[] { "Fix", "--colour", "red" }) is null);
Dojo.Check("flags but no title gives null", ParseAdd(new[] { "--tag", "bug" }) is null);
Dojo.Check("no arguments gives null", ParseAdd(new string[0]) is null);
var dojoTask = AddTask(dojoAssistant, new AddRequest("Fix login", "Bug", "web", 45));
Dojo.Eq("AddTask gives the first task id 1", 1, dojoTask.Id);
Dojo.Eq<string?>("AddTask sets the tag (normalised by your TaskItem)", "bug", dojoTask.Tag);
Dojo.Eq("the assistant now holds the task", 1, dojoAssistant.All.Count);

if (!int.TryParse(t.Substring(0, h), out hours) || hours < 0) return false;

public TaskItem(int id, string title, int estimateMinutes = 0)
if (id < 1) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(id), "Task ids start at 1.");
if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(title)) throw new ArgumentException("A task needs a title.", nameof(title));
if (estimateMinutes < 0) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(estimateMinutes), "An estimate cannot be negative.");

string projectPart = Project is { Length: > 0 } p ? $" @{p}" : "";
string duePart = Due is DateOnly d ? $" (due {d:ddd d MMM})" : "";
if (Done) throw new InvalidOperationException("A finished task cannot be started.");
if (at < StartedAt) throw new ArgumentException("A timer cannot stop before it started.", nameof(at));
if (minutes < 1) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(minutes), "Log at least one minute.");

public static bool CanMove(Status from, Status to) => (from, to) switch
(Status.Doing, Status.Todo or Status.Blocked or Status.Done) => true,

steps.explain: A list pattern describes the *shape* of the arguments: a flag, its value, and whatever follows. Each `case` reads like the rule it implements, and an argument list that matches no rule is refused instead of half-parsed.
